Answer: A
Reason: Figure 1b demonstrates a dramatic rightward displacement of the cardiac silhouette into the right hemithorax with an abnormal, elongated contour compared to the normal position in Figure 1a. This finding is diagnostic of cardiac herniation through a pericardial defect, a known post-surgical complication that causes acute haemodynamic compromise due to torsion and obstruction of the great vessels.
